questions.q: The integral $∫ \left(\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)x + \left(\dfrac{2}{x}\right)x\right)\log_{2}xdx$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$I = ∫ \left(\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)x + \left(\dfrac{2}{x}\right)x\right)\log_{2}xdx$

Now, Let \left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)x = t$

$⇒ x\log_{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) = \log_{2}t$

$⇒ x\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) \cdot \log_{2}e = \log_{\mathrm{e}}t \cdot \log_{2}e$

On differentiating both sides we get :
$\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) + x \cdot \dfrac{2}{x} \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{t}\dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$⇒ \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) + 1 = \dfrac{1}{t}\dfrac{dt}{dx}$

Then solution is not possible as \text{ and } there is no proper substitution.

Note: This question was bonus in Jee \text{ and } Mains 2023 April session.

$

Let $\sin x + \cos x = t$

questions.q: If& $I\left(x\right) = ∫ e^{\sin^{2}x} \left($\cos x \sin 2x - \sin x\right)dx$~and~I\left($0\right) = 1$, then~I\left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) \text{ and } is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$I\left(x\right) = ∫ e^{\sin^{2}x}\left(\cos x \sin 2x - \sin x\right)dx$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ∫ e^{\sin^{2}x}\left(\cos x - \dfrac{1}{2\cos x}\right)\sin 2xdx$

Now let,~$\sin^{2}x = t ⇒ \sin 2xdx = dt$

$I\left(x\right) = ∫ e^{t}\left(\sqrt{1 - t} - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{1 - t}}\right)dt$

Now comparing with,

$I\left(x\right) = ∫ e^{t}\left(f\left(t\right) + f^{'}\left(t\right)\right)dt = e^{t}f\left(t\right) + c$

Here,~$f\left(t\right) = \sqrt{1 - t} \text{ and } f^{'}\left(t\right) = - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{1 - t}}$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = e^{t}\sqrt{1 - t} + c = e^{\sin^{2}x} \cdot \cos x + c$

Now using,~$I\left(0\right) = 1 ⇒ c = 0$

Hence, the value of~$I\left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}e\dfrac{3}{4}$

questions.q: $∫ sec^{2}x \cdot cot\dfrac{4}{3}xdx$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given integral can be written as

$I = ∫ \dfrac{\sec^{2}x}{\left(\tan x\right)\dfrac{4}{3}}dx$

Let~$\tan x = t$

$⇒ \sec^{2}xdx = dt$

$⇒ I = ∫ t^{- \dfrac{4}{3}}dt$

Using~$∫ x^{n}dx = \dfrac{xn + 1}{n + 1} + C,$~we get

$I = t^{- \dfrac{1}{3}}\left(- \dfrac{1}{3}\right) + C$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{3}{t\dfrac{1}{3}} + C$

$⇒ I = - 3\tan^{- \dfrac{1}{3}}x + C .$

questions.q: Let $\int x^3 \sin x \mathrm{~d} x=g(x)+C$, where $C$ is the constant of integration. If $8\left(g\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)+g^{\prime}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)=\alpha \pi^3+\beta \pi^2+\gamma, \alpha, \beta, \gamma \in Z$, then $\alpha+\beta-\gamma$ equals :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \int x^3 \sin x d x=-x^3 \cos x+\int 3 x^2 \cos x d x \\
& =-x^3 \cos x+3 x^2 \sin x-\int 6 x \sin x d x \\
& =-x^3 \cos x+3 x^2 \sin x+6 x \cos x-6 \sin x+c
\end{aligned}$ So $g(x)=-x^3 \cos x+3 x^2 \sin x+6 x \cos x-6 \sin x$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{g}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{3 \pi^2}{4}-6 \\
& \mathrm{~g}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=-3 \mathrm{x}^2 \cos \mathrm{x}+\mathrm{x}^3 \sin \mathrm{x}+6 \cos \mathrm{x}-6 \cos \mathrm{x} \\
& \mathrm{~g}^{\prime}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi^3}{8} \\
& 8\left(\mathrm{~g}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)+\mathrmg^{\prime}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)=\pi^3+6 \pi^2-48
\end{aligned}$$ So $\alpha+\beta-\gamma=55$

questions.q: If $∫ x^{5}e^{- 4x^{3}}dx = \dfrac{1}{48}e^{- 4x^{3}}f  \left(x\right) + C$, where $C$ is a constant of integration, then $f\left(x\right) is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,& $I = ∫ x^{5}e^{- 4x^{3}}dx$~

Let,~$- 4x^{3} = t ⇒ - 12x^{2}dx = dt$

$⇒ I = ∫ \left(- \dfrac{t}{4}\right)e^{t}\left(- \dfrac{dt}{12}\right) = \dfrac{1}{48} ∫ te^{t}dt$

$= \dfrac{1}{48}\left[te^{t} - ∫ e^{t}dt\right] = \dfrac{\left(t - 1\right)e^{t}}{48} + C = \dfrac{\left(- 4x^{3} - 1\right)e^{- 4x^{3}}}{48} + C,$
where~$C$~is the constant of integration.

Hence,~$f\left(x\right) = - 4x^{3} - 1$

questions.q: The integral $∫ \dfrac{\left(x^{8} - x^{2}\right)dx}{\left(x^{12} + 3x^{6} + 1\right)\tan^{- 1}\left(x^{3} + \dfrac{1}{x3}\right)}$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, $I = ∫ \dfrac{x^{8} - x^{2}}{\left(x^{12} + 3x^{6} + 1\right)\tan^{- 1}\left(x^{3} + \dfrac{1}{x3}\right)}dx$

Putting, $\tan^{- 1}\left(x^{3} + \dfrac{1}{x3}\right) = t$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{1 + \left(x^{3} + \dfrac{1}{x3}\right)2} \cdot \left(3x^{2} - \dfrac{3}{x4}\right)dx = dt$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{1 + \left(x^{6} + \dfrac{1}{x6} + 2\right)} \cdot \left(3x^{2} - \dfrac{3}{x4}\right)dx = dt$

$⇒ \dfrac{x6}{x^{12} + 3x^{6} + 1} \cdot \dfrac{3x^{6} - 3}{x4}dx = dt$

$⇒ \left(x^{8} - x^{2}\right)x^{12} + 3x^{6} + 1dx = \dfrac{dt}{3}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{3} ∫ \dfrac{1}{t}dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{3}log | t | + C$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{3}\log \left|\tan^{- 1}\left(x^{3} + \dfrac{1}{x3}\right)\right| + C$

$⇒ I = \log \left|\tan^{- 1} \left($x^{3} + $\dfrac{1}{x3}\right)\right|\dfrac{1}{3} +$C$

Hence optin \left($A\right)$ is correct

$

questions.q: The integral& $∫ \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(\cos x - \sin x\right)\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{3}\sin 2x\right)dx$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& $I = ∫ \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(\cos x - \sin x\right)\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{3}\sin 2x\right)dx$

Multiplying by~$\dfrac{3}{2}$~in numerator and denominator, we get

$I = ∫ \left(\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(\cos x - \sin x\right)\left(\dfrac{3}{2} + \sin 2x\right)dx$

$= ∫ \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(\cos x - \sin x\right)}{sin\dfrac{π}{3} + \sin 2x}dx$

$= ∫ \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\cos x - \dfrac{1}{2}\cos x - \dfrac{3}{2}\sin x + \dfrac{1}{2}\sin x\right)2\sin \left(x + \dfrac{π}{6}\right)\cos \left(x - \dfrac{π}{6}\right)dx$

$= ∫ \left(\cos \left(x - \dfrac{π}{6}\right) - \sin \left(x + \dfrac{π}{6}\right)\right)2\sin \left(x + \dfrac{π}{6}\right)\cos \left(x - \dfrac{π}{6}\right)dx$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \left(∫ $\dfrac{dx}{\sin \left(x + $\dfrac{π}{6}\right)}$ - ∫ $\dfrac{dx}{\cos \left(x - \dfrac{π}{6}\right)}\right)

=\dfrac{1}{2} \left($∫ cosec \left($x + \dfrac{π}{6}\right)dx - ∫ \sec \left($x - \dfrac{π}{6}\right)dx\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\ln \left|$tan\dfrac{x + \dfrac{π}{6}}{2}\right|\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\ln \left|$tan\dfrac{x - \dfrac{π}{6}}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right|\right) +C$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln \left|$\dfrac{\tan \left(\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{π}{12}\right)}{\tan \left(\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{π}{6}\right)}\right| +C$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{x}{\left(1 + x\right)2}dx$

Let~$x = \tan^{2}\theta$

$dx = 2tan\theta\sec^{2}\thetad\theta$

$f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{tan\theta}{\left(1 + \tan^{2}\theta\right)2} . 2tan\theta\sec^{2}\thetad\theta$

$f\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{tan\theta}{\sec^{4}\theta} . 2tan\theta\sec^{2}\thetad\theta$

$f\left(x\right) = ∫ 2\tan^{2}\theta . \cos^{2}\thetad\theta$

$f\left(x\right) = ∫ 2\sin^{2}\thetad\theta$

$f\left(x\right) = ∫ \left(1 - \cos 2\theta\right)d\theta$

$f\left(x\right) = \theta - \dfrac{\sin 2\theta}{2} + C = \theta - \dfrac{tan\theta}{1 + \tan^{2}\theta} + C$

$f\left(x\right) = \tan^{- 1}\sqrt{x} - \dfrac{x}{1 + x} + C$

Now,~$f\left(3\right) - f\left(1\right) = \tan^{−}\sqrt{3} - \dfrac{3}{1 + 3} - \tan^{- 1}\sqrt{1} + \dfrac{1}{1 + 1}$

$= \dfrac{π}{3} - \dfrac{π}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{π}{12} + \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{3}{4}$

questions.q: The integral $∫ \dfrac{1}{( x - 1{)}^{3} ( x + 2{)}^{5}4}dx$ is equal to : (where $C$ is a constant of integration)
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$I = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{( x - 1{)}^{3} ( x + 2{)}^{5}4}$

$I = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{( x - 1{)}^{\dfrac{3}{4}} ( x + 2{)}^{\dfrac{5}{4}}}$

$I = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{( x - 1{)}^{2}\left(\dfrac{x + 2}{x - 1}\right)\dfrac{5}{4}}$

Let~$\dfrac{x + 2}{x - 1} = t$

Differentiate on both sides

$\dfrac{\left(x - 1\right) - \left(x + 2\right)}{\left(x - 1\right)2} . dx = dt$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{\left(x - 1\right)2} = \dfrac{- dt}{3}$

$I = \dfrac{- 1}{3} ∫ \dfrac{dt}{\left(t\right)\dfrac{5}{4}}$

$= \dfrac{- 1}{3}\dfrac{t\dfrac{- 5}{4} + 1}{1 - \dfrac{5}{4}} + C$

$= \dfrac{4}{3}t\dfrac{- 1}{4} + C$

$= \dfrac{4}{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{t}\right)\dfrac{1}{4} + C$

$= \dfrac{4}{3}\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 2}\right)\dfrac{1}{4} + C$

questions.q: Let& $I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{x + 1}{x  \left(1 + xe^{x}\right)2}dx, x > 0 .$~If~$\lim_{x \to \iinfty}I\left($x\right) = 0$~then~I\left($1\right)$& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{x + 1}{x\left(1 + xe^{x}\right)2}dx$

Now let~$1 + xe^{x} = t$

$⇒ e^{x}\left(x + 1\right)dx = dt$

So,~$I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{1}{\left(t - 1\right)t^{2}}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{\left(1 - t^{2}\right) + t^{2}}{\left(t - 1\right)t^{2}}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{- \left(t + 1\right)}{t2} + \dfrac{1}{t - 1}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ∫ - \dfrac{1}{t} - \dfrac{1}{t2} + \dfrac{1}{t - 1}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = - \ln t + \dfrac{1}{t} + \ln \left(t - 1\right) + C$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = \ln \left(\dfrac{xe^{x}}{xe^{x} + 1}\right) + \dfrac{1}{xe^{x} + 1} + C$

Also given,$\lim_{x \to \infty}I\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \infty}I\left(x\right) = \lim_{x \to \infty} \left[\ln \left($1 - $\dfrac{1}{xe^{x} + 1}\right) + \dfrac{1}{xe^{x} + 1} +$C\right]$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \infty}$I \left(x\right) = \lleft[\ln \left(1 - 0\right) + 0 + C]$

$⇒ C = 0$

Now finding,

$I\left(1\right) = \ln \left(\dfrac{e}{e + 1}) + \dfrac{1}{e + 1} =$1 + $\dfrac{1}{e + 1} -$\ln ( e + 1 )$

$⇒ I \left($1\right) = $\dfrac{e + 2}{e + 1} --$\ln \left($e + 1\right)$

$

questions.q: Let& $I\left(x\right) = ∫ \sqrt{\dfrac{x + 7}{x}}dx$~and~$I\left(9\right) = 12 + 7\log_{\mathrm{e}}7$. If~$I\left(1\right) = \alpha + 7\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(1 + 2\sqrt{2}\right),$~then~${α}^{4}$& is equal to _____.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$I\left(x\right) = ∫ \sqrt{\dfrac{x + 7}{x}}dx$

Now let,~$\dfrac{x + 7}{x} = t^{2} ⇒ - \dfrac{7}{x2}dx = 2tdt$

$⇒ dx = \dfrac{- 14t}{\left(t^{2} - 1\right)2}dt$

So,~$I\left(x\right) = - 14 ∫ \dfrac{t2}{ \left(t^{2} - 1\right)2}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = - 14 ∫ dt\left(t^{2} + $\dfrac{1}{t2} -$2\right)$

$⇒ $I \left($x\right) = \dfrac{- 14}{2}∫ \left[\left($1 - \dfrac{1}{t2}\right)\left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)2 - 4 + \left($1 + \dfrac{1}{t2}\right)\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right)2\right]dt$

$⇒ $I\left($x\right) = - $7\left(\ddfrac{1}{4}\ln \left|$\dfrac{t + \dfrac{1}{t} - 2}{t + \dfrac{1}{t} + 2}\right| - \dfrac{1}{t - \dfrac{1}{t}}\right) +$c$

Now when~$x = 9, t = $\dfrac{4}{3}

$⇒ $I \left($9\right) = 12 + 7 \timesln7 = \dfrac{- 77}{4}$\ln \left(\dfrac{1}{7}\right)$2 + 7 \times $\dfrac{12}{7} +$c$

$⇒ c = $\dfrac{7}{2}$\ln 7$

Now when~$x = 1, t = $2\sqrt{2}

$⇒ $I \left($1\right) = + $\ddfrac{7}{4}\ln \left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{2} + 1}{2\sqrt{2} - 1})$2 + 7 \times $\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{7} + \dfrac{7}{2}$\ln 7$

$⇒ I\left(1\right) = $\d$dfrac{7}{2}\ln \left(\dfrac{\left(2\sqrt{2} + 1\right)2}{7}) +$++2\sqrt{2} + \dfrac{7}{2}$\ln 7$

$⇒ I\left(1\right) = $7ln\lleft(2\sqrt{2} +1) - \dfrac{7}{2}\ln 7 + 2\sqrt{2} + \dfrac{7}{2}\ln 7$

$⇒ $\alpha $==2\sqrt{2}$⇒ {α}^{4} = 64$

$

questions.q: If& $∫ \sqrt{\sec 2x - 1}dx = \alpha\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left|\cos 2x + \beta + \sqrt{\cos 2x\left(1 + cos\dfrac{1}{β}x\right)}\right|$~ ~$+$ constant, then $\beta - \alpha$ is equal to ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$∫ \sqrt{\sec 2x - 1}dx = \alpha\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left|\cos 2x + \beta + \sqrt{\cos 2x\left(1 + cos\dfrac{1}{β}x\right)}\right| + C$

Now solving~$L . H . S$~we get,

$∫ \sqrt{\sec 2x - 1}dx = ∫ \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - \cos 2x}{\cos 2x}}dx$

$⇒ ∫ \sqrt{\sec 2x - 1}dx = \sqrt{2} ∫ \dfrac{\sin x}{2\cos^{2}x - 1}dx$

Now let~$\cos x = t ⇒ - sinxdx = dt$

$⇒ ∫ \sqrt{\sec 2x - 1}dx = - \sqrt{2} ∫ \dfrac{dt}{2t^{2} - 1}$

$⇒ ∫ \sqrt{\sec 2x - 1}dx = - ln | \sqrt{2}\cos x + \sqrt{\cos 2x} | + C$

$= - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln \left|2\cos^{2}x + \cos 2x + 2\sqrt{\cos 2x} \cdot \sqrt{2}\cos x\right| + C$

$= - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln \left|\cos 2x + \dfrac{1}{2} + \sqrt{\cos 2x} \cdot \sqrt{1 + \cos 2x}\right| + C$

Now on comparing with~$∫ \sqrt{\sec 2x - 1}dx = \alpha\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left|\cos 2x + \beta + \sqrt{\cos 2x\left(1 + cos\dfrac{1}{β}x\right)}\right| + C$

We get,~$\beta = \dfrac{1}{2}, \alpha = - \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \beta - \alpha = 1$

questions.q: $∫ \dfrac{2e^{x} + 3e^{- x}}{4e^{x} + 7e^{- x}}dx = \dfrac{1}{14}\left(ux + v\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(4e^{x} + 7e^{- x}\right)\right) + C$, where $C$ is a constant of integration, then $u + v$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$I = ∫ \dfrac{2e^{x} + 3e^{- x}}{4e^{x} + 7e^{- x}}dx = ∫ \dfrac{2e^{x} + 3}{4e^{2x} + 7}dx$
Here $2e^{2x} + 3 = A \left(8e^{2x}\right) + B \left($4e^{2x} + 7\right)$
$⇒ 2e^{2x} + 3 = ( 8A + 4B ) e^{2x} + 7B$
$⇒ B = $\dfrac{3}{7}$ \text{ and } A = $\dfrac{1}{28}
$I = ∫ $\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{28}\left(8e^{2x}\right) + \dfrac{3}{7}\left(4e^{2x} + 7\right)}{4e^{2x} + 7}$dx$
$I = $\ddfrac{1}{28}\ln \left|4e^{2x} + 7\right| + \dfrac{3}{7}x + C$
$I = \dfrac{1}{28}ln ∣ e^{x} \left(4e^{x} + 7e^{- x} ∣ + $\dfrac{3}{7}$x + C\right$
$⇒ u = $\dfrac{13}{2}$ \text{ and } v = $\dfrac{1}{2}
$⇒ u + v = $\dfrac{13}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} =$7$

questions.q: For real numbers $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ and $\delta,$ if~$∫ \dfrac{\left(x^{2} - 1\right) + \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x^{2} + 1}{x}\right)}{\left(x^{4} + 3x^{2} + 1\right)\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x^{2} + 1}{x}\right)}dx = \alpha\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x^{2} + 1}{x}\right)\right) + \beta\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\gamma\left(x^{2} - 1\right)}{x}\right) + \delta\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x^{2} + 1}{x}\right) + C$ where $C$ is an arbitrary constant, then the value of $10 ( \alpha + \beta\gamma + \delta )$ is equal to ______ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$∫ \dfrac{\left(x^{2} - 1\right)dx}{\left(x^{4} + 3x^{2} + 1\right)\tan^{- 1}\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)} + ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x^{4} + 3x^{2} + 1}$

$∫ \dfrac{\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{x2}\right)dx}{\left(\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)2 + 1\right)\tan^{- 1}\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)} + \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{\left(x^{2} + 1\right) - \left(x^{2} - 1\right)dx}{x^{4} + 3x^{2} + 1}$

Put~$\tan^{- 1}\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right) = t$

$∫ \dfrac{dt}{t} + \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x2}\right)dx}{\left(x - \dfrac{1}{x}\right)2 + 5} - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{x2}\right)dx}{\left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)2 + 1}$

Put~$x - \dfrac{1}{x} = y, x + \dfrac{1}{x} = z$

$\log_{\mathrm{e}}t + \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{dy}{y^{2} + 5} - \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{dz}{z^{2} + 1}$

$= \log_{\mathrm{e}}\tan^{- 1} \left($x + $\dfrac{1}{x}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x^{2} - 1}{\sqrt{5}x}\right)

$- $\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x^{2} + 1}{x}\right) +$C$

\alpha =$1, $\beta = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}, \gamma = \dfrac{1}{5}, \delta = \dfrac{- 1}{2}

or~\alpha =$1, $\beta = \dfrac{- 1}{2\sqrt{5}}, \gamma = \dfrac{- 1}{5}, \delta = \dfrac{- 1}{2}

$10 ( $\alpha + \beta\gamma + \delta ) =$10\left($1 + $\dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) =$6$
